## Interpretation table

| Level | Question | Result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Mixing mechanism on planted rugged controls | PCD best gradient error (6.80) and only meaningful mode coverage (0.33); QeMCMC second tier (18.86), ahead of Gibbs/MH/PT. | G2's static-landscape QeMCMC advantage does not transfer automatically into the training loop: with 32 fresh-chain proposals per update, chain persistence across updates beats per-step mixing quality. A finding, not a failure — it defined the Stage-2 question. |
| B-easy | Transfer to easy synthetic learning | PCD 13.90 < QeMCMC 16.49 < mh-local 18.94 < Gibbs 19.54 < mh-uniform 20.52 < PT 22.98. | Same persistence-dominated ordering as Level A; QeMCMC is the best fresh-chain sampler but trails PCD. |
| B-hard | Transfer to hard synthetic learning | PCD 13.20 < QeMCMC 16.41 < mh-local 18.11 < Gibbs 18.82 < mh-uniform 19.61 < PT 21.85. | Consistent with B-easy; harder couplings widen no gaps qualitatively. |
| C | Transfer to real crop latent codes | **QeMCMC best of all approximate samplers: 5.30 vs mh-uniform 7.37, PCD 11.48, Gibbs 13.63, PT 15.71** — no per-seed overlap with the runner-up (5.26/5.30/5.34 vs 7.00/7.46/7.64). | The headline: the quantum sampler measurably improves the training signal on real image-derived codes, exceeding the §8 modal expectation (a plug-in tie). The causal chain holds through validation NLL; classification compresses at the last link, as pre-registered. |

## 1. Negative-phase gradient error (primary)

The pre-registered primary metric, and the informative one at this budget
(see §3 caveat). Mean over 3 seeds, all 100 updates, from the causal-chain
table above:

- **Level C:** QeMCMC 5.30 — best approximate sampler by a wide, seed-robust
  margin (next best mh-uniform 7.37; PCD 11.48). This is the Stage-1
  headline and the G4 entry-condition signal (≈3× spread by sampler).
- **Levels A / B-easy / B-hard:** PCD dominates (6.80 / 13.90 / 13.20);
  QeMCMC is consistently second tier (18.86 / 16.49 / 16.41), ahead of the
  remaining fresh-chain classical samplers everywhere.
- Reading: sampler identity changes the EBM training signal, and WHICH
  sampler wins is landscape-dependent — persistence wins on planted/synthetic
  ruggedness, per-step proposal quality wins on the real smooth crop codes.

## 2. ESS and autocorrelation per proposal step

QeMCMC posts the best magnetization mixing on every level (e.g. Level C:
magnetization IAT 2.18 vs 3.03–7.20 for classical samplers; ESS/proposal
0.55 vs ≤0.45), consistent with the G2 static-landscape result. Energy-ESS
ordering is less separated and PCD's persistent chains make its per-update
IAT non-comparable in the fresh-chain sense (censored-IAT caveat from the
G2 amendment applies). Mixing quality alone did not predict in-loop
gradient accuracy on A/B — the central Stage-1 lesson.

## 3. TV, KL, and mode coverage

Metric caveat recorded at the G3 verdict: against the exact Boltzmann
distribution over 2^20 states, 32-sample empirical TV is near its ceiling
by construction (≈1 for every fresh-chain sampler; PCD's persistent chains
reach 0.59 on Level A), and KL/mode-coverage are similarly near-degenerate
(mode coverage 0 to 0.33, meaningfully nonzero only for PCD on Level A).
These columns are reported for completeness but are not informative at this
budget; gradient error (a moment estimate, valid at small sample size) is
the §7 metric that carries the comparison.

## 4. Training stability and convergence

All 84 runs completed stably (no divergence, no budget-guard trips). Final
train-NLL std across seeds is small for the top samplers (e.g. Level C:
≤0.05 for QeMCMC/PCD/mh-uniform) and largest for PT (which collapsed on
Level C, final val NLL 16.05 and Macro-F1 0.26). Gradient error drifts
upward over training for all fresh-chain samplers as the learned couplings
sharpen the landscape (e.g. QeMCMC Level A 3.78 → 20.74); PCD's drift is
much flatter — the same persistence signature that decides §1.

## 5. Held-out exact NLL

The causal chain holds one link down: better gradients → better held-out
NLL. Level C best-val NLL: exact 14.45 < QeMCMC 14.72 < mh-uniform 14.84 <
PCD 14.97 < Gibbs 15.12 < PT 15.41 — same ordering as gradient error for
the top three. Levels A/B: PCD best among approximate samplers (A: 2.12 vs
QeMCMC 3.19; B-easy: 6.58 vs 8.20; B-hard: 10.82 vs 11.47), mirroring §1.

## 6. Downstream classification (last link)

Differences compress at the classification link, as pre-registered. Level C
test Macro-F1 (3-seed means): exact 0.509 > PCD 0.463 ≈ mh-uniform 0.458 ≈
QeMCMC 0.450 > Gibbs/mh-local ≈ 0.43 > PT 0.259 (collapsed). B-easy/B-hard
reach 0.95–1.00 for all top samplers (the synthetic task is learnable by
all); Level A classification is a small side quantity with one degenerate
seed and is not load-bearing. No downstream headline is claimed from these
numbers, per the prereg.
